name: – Li Andersson – Amendments by the committee responsible – separate votes – Am 17/1
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: To enhance employability and quality job creation and transitions, Member States should ensure an effective individual right to accessible, quality education and training during working time and at no cost to the worker. Such a right can include, where appropriate, individual learning accounts, reliable training quality assessments and micro-credentials. They should enable everyone to anticipate and better adapt to labour market needs, in particular through continuous upskilling and reskilling and the provision of integrated career guidance and counselling. Member States should raise awareness, including among employers, of the importance of lifelong-learning-friendly work, and ensure that employment, skills, industrial and investment policies are mutually reinforcing and informed by reliable labour-market intelligence. They should also support the reallocation of workers towards sectors and occupations with stronger employment prospects, while taking into account regional and sectoral shortages and the specific challenges of rural, peripheral and less-developed regions affected by ageing, outward migration and a declining working-age population. Member States should ensure that all formal qualifications and credentials offer clear pathways for further studies or progression.
